newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-SWEDISH PART-TIMERS SHUN MILAN FASHION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDISH PART-TIMERS SHUN MILAN FASHION.

text.p: Swedish part-timers IFK Gothenburg fought back with two late goals on Wednesday to beat AC Milan 2-1 in the European Champions'league and plunge their fans into despair at the team's latest collapse.

Milan, resting on their distinguished laurels after taking a 52nd minute lead through majestic Liberian striker George Weah, suddenly found themselves facing the real possiblity of being knocked out of Europe after the Swedes scored twice in 10 minutes late in the game.

Uruguayan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez, sensing the hysteria awaiting him back in Italy, appealed for calm: "It's time for cool heads. The team decision to pull everything into defence after taking the lead was fatal."
By Milan's standards the current season has started disastrously, with mediocre performances in Europe and the Italian league, including a 3-0 defeat at the hands of Rome on Saturday.

But a capacity crowd of 42,450 went home delighted that their team, crowned Swedish champions for the fourth successive season just four days ago had won their first match in Group D and kept alive their hopes of reaching the last eight.
The game started in frenetic fashion with Weah and Marco Simone looking to take up where they left off in Norway two weeks ago when they put four past Rosenborg.

Weah and Simone indulged in a 50-metre passing exchange that eventually put the striding Liberian through. Stranded Swedish international goalkeeper Thomas Ravelli could only watch as Weah's delicate shot hit the outside of the post.

Four minutes later 20-year-old Tomas Locatelli forced Ravelli to pull of a dramatic save with a carefully flighted left foot shot but Milan's midfield was already showing signs of immaturity against the efficient Swedes.
But Milan, playing as if powerful club president Silvio Berlusconi was literally breathing down their necks, were far from the smooth and precise unit they can be at their best.
Pouring rain greeted the players as they walked out onto the Ullevi stadium for the second half and it transformed the pitch into a skating rink, making life equally difficult for both teams.
Milan took advantage of the greasy pitch in the 54th minute when defender Jonas Olsson missed a skidding ball, presenting Weah with the chance to tuck the ball gracefullypast Ravelli.
The stubborn Swedes, who had troubled Milan all evening, fought back and substitute Erik Wahlstedt had only been on the field for a minute when he headed home an Olsson cross to equalise.
Olsson showed all the skill of his Italian opposition, turning veteran Italian full-back Paolo Maldini inside out to cross to Wahlstedt.
Ten minutes later the Italian team was enraged when Polish referee Wojcik Ryszard granted a Niclas Alexandersson goal that thye claimed was offside.
Replays showed, however, the linesman's decision was correct and that the Italian back four had been caught flat.

IFK Gothenburg - 1-Thomas Ravelli; 13-Mikael Nilsson, 4-Jonas Olsson, 6-Teddy Lucic, 22-Stefan Landberg (3-Magnus Johansson, 78); 9-Niclas Alexandersson, 11-Stefan Lindqvist, 16-Jesper Blomqvist; 19-Magnus Erlingmark, 10-Stefan Pettersson (18-Erik Wahlstedt, 73) 14-Andreas Andersson.

AC Milan - 1-Sebastiano Rossi; 2-Christian Panucci, 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 3-Paolo Maldini, 8-Marcel Desailly; 4-Demetrio Albertini, 15-Massimo Ambrosini, 16-Tomas Locatelli (14-Michael Reiziger, 70), 20-Zvonimir Boban; 9-George Weah, 23-Marco Simone (19-Christophe Dugarry, 78).
